c5582e8b-3870-5a32-b15e-62b8f8306ce6.title: Differentiating Inverse Trigonometric Functions Using the Product or Quotient Rule

e-206.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of arcsine is

$$
\frac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(\arcsin x) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(3{x}^{2})) \\  & =5\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(3{x}^{2})^{2}}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{x}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{5}{\sqrt{1-9{x}^{4}}}\cdot (6x) \\  & =\frac{30x}{\sqrt{1-9{x}^{4}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

e-203.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of arccosine is

$$
\frac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(\arccos x) = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccos}⁡(5-8x)) \\  & =-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(5-8x)^{2}}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5-8x) \\  & =-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(25-80x+64{x}^{2})}}\cdot (-8) \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{80x-24-64{x}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{4(20x-6-16{x}^{2})}} \\  & =\frac{8}{2\sqrt{20x-6-16{x}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{4}{\sqrt{20x-6-16{x}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

e-202.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of arctangent is

$$
\frac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(\arctan x) = \dfrac{1}{1+x^2}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-7x)) \\  & =\frac{1}{1+(-7x)^{2}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-7x) \\  & =\frac{1}{1+49{x}^{2}}\cdot (-7) \\  & =-\frac{7}{1+49{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

e-204.knowledge_point: Differentiating Inverse Trigonometric Functions Using the Product or Quotient Rule
e-204.worked_solution:
Applying the product rule and using the formula for the derivative of $\arccos x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x\operatorname{arccos}⁡x) & =x\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccos}⁡x)+\operatorname{arccos}⁡x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =x\cdot (-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}})+\operatorname{arccos}⁡x\cdot 1 \\  & =-\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}+\operatorname{arccos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Using the chain rule, f′(x)=8·e^x/√(1−(e^x)^2)=8e^x/√(1−e^{2x}), which matches option e.

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of arcsine is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[8\operatorname{arcsin}⁡({e}^{x})] \\  & =8\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{({e}^{x})}^{2}}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x}) \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{1-{e}^{2x}}}\cdot {e}^{x} \\  & =\frac{8{e}^{x}}{\sqrt{1-{e}^{2x}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.html:
Question 1
?

Calculate f′(x) for f(x)=8arcsin⁡(ex).

a
−8ex1+ex
b
ex81+e2x
c
−8e2x1−ex
d
ex81−e2x
e
8ex1−e2x
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The formula for the derivative of arcsine is ddx(arcsin⁡x)=11−x2.

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we get

f′(x)=ddx[8arcsin⁡(ex)]=8⋅11−(ex)2⋅ddx(ex)=81−e2x⋅ex=8ex1−e2x.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms the chain rule gives f′(x)=8e^x/√(1−e^{2x}), matching option e. The submitted option b was incorrect.

content.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of arcsine is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[8\operatorname{arcsin}⁡({e}^{x})] \\  & =8\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{({e}^{x})}^{2}}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x}) \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{1-{e}^{2x}}}\cdot {e}^{x} \\  & =\frac{8{e}^{x}}{\sqrt{1-{e}^{2x}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 2
?

Calculate dydx for y=arcsin⁡x4−14x.

a
 14x2−1−14x2
b
 141−x2+12x2
c
 14x2−1+14x2
d
 141−x2−12x2
e
141−x2+14x2
Submit

decision.explanation: Differentiate each term: (arcsin x)/4 gives 1/(4√(1−x²)), and −(1/4)x⁻¹ gives +(1/4)x⁻². Their sum matches option e.

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of arcsine is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x}{4}-\frac{1}{4x}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x)+\frac{1}{4{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}+\frac{1}{4{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{4\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}+\frac{1}{4{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

Calculate dydx for y=arcsin⁡x4−14x.

a
 14x2−1−14x2
b
 141−x2+12x2
c
 14x2−1+14x2
d
 141−x2−12x2
e
141−x2+14x2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The formula for the derivative of arcsine is ddx(arcsin⁡x)=11−x2.

Using the formula above, we get

dydx=ddx(arcsin⁡x4−14x)=14⋅ddx(arcsin⁡x)+14x2=14⋅11−x2+14x2=141−x2+14x2.

content.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of arcsine is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x}{4}-\frac{1}{4x}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x)+\frac{1}{4{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}+\frac{1}{4{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{4\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}+\frac{1}{4{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Calculate dydx for y=5+9arcsin⁡x.

a
91−x2
b
191+x2
c
−91+x2
d
91+x2
e
−91−x2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The formula for the derivative of arcsine is ddx(arcsin⁡x)=11−x2.

Using the formula above, we get

dydx=ddx(5+9arcsin⁡x)=0+9⋅ddx(arcsin⁡x)=0+9⋅11−x2=91−x2.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms that the constant differentiates to 0 and 9 arcsin(x) differentiates to 9/√(1−x²). Therefore option a is correct; option e has the wrong sign.

content.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of arcsine is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5+9\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x) \\  & =0+9\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x) \\  & =0+9\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{9}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

a
 41−2x2
b
 81−4x2
c
 41+4x2
d
 81−2x2
e
 81+2x2

decision.explanation: Using the chain rule, f′(x)=4·2/√(1−(2x)²)=8/√(1−4x²), which matches option b.

after.name: Question 4
after.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of arcsine is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(2x)) \\  & =4\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(2x)) \\  & =4\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(2x)^{2}}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2x) \\  & =4\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-4{x}^{2}}}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{1-4{x}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}

Question 4
?

Find f′(x) for f(x)=4arcsin⁡(2x).

a
 41−2x2
b
 81−4x2
c
 41+4x2
d
 81−2x2
e
 81+2x2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The formula for the derivative of arcsine is ddx(arcsin⁡x)=11−x2.

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we get

f′(x)=ddx(4arcsin⁡(2x))=4⋅ddx(arcsin⁡(2x))=4⋅11−(2x)2⋅ddx(2x)=4⋅11−4x2⋅2=81−4x2.

content.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of arcsine is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(2x)) \\  & =4\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(2x)) \\  & =4\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(2x)^{2}}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2x) \\  & =4\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-4{x}^{2}}}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{1-4{x}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 5
?

Find f′(x) for f(x)=arcsin5⁡(4x).

a
4arcsin4⁡(4x)1−16x2
b
20arcsin4⁡(4x)1−16x2
c
20arcsin2⁡(4x)1−4x2
d
5arcsin4⁡(4x)1−4x2
e
5arcsin4⁡(2x)1−16x2
Submit

decision.explanation: Apply the power rule and chain rule: f′(x)=5(arcsin(4x))⁴·4/√(1−(4x)²)=20(arcsin(4x))⁴/√(1−16x²). This matches option b.

after.name: Question 5
after.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of arcsine is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[{arcsin}^{5}⁡(4x)] \\  & =5{arcsin}^{4}⁡(4x)\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(4x)] \\  & =5{arcsin}^{4}⁡(4x)\cdot [\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(4x)^{2}}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4x)] \\  & =5{arcsin}^{4}⁡(4x)\cdot [\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(4x)^{2}}}\cdot 4] \\  & =5{arcsin}^{4}⁡(4x)\cdot \frac{4}{\sqrt{1-16{x}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{20{arcsin}^{4}⁡(4x)}{\sqrt{1-16{x}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Question 7
?

Calculate f′(x) for f(x)=5x+4arccos⁡x.

a
5x+41−x2
b
4−51−x2
c
5−41−x2
d
5+41−x2
e
5−4x1−x2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The formula for the derivative of arccosine is ddx(arccos⁡x)=−11−x2.

Using the formula above, we get f′(x)=ddx(5x+4arccos⁡x)=5+4⋅ddx(arccos⁡x)=5+4(−11−x2)=5−41−x2.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms (5x)′=5 and (4 arccos x)′=−4/√(1−x²), so option c is correct.

content.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of arccosine is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccos}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5x+4\operatorname{arccos}⁡x) \\  & =5+4\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccos}⁡x) \\  & =5+4(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}) \\  & =5-\frac{4}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of arccosine is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccos}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2x-5\operatorname{arccos}⁡x) \\  & =2-5\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccos}⁡x) \\  & =2-5(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}) \\  & =2+\frac{5}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Since (arccos x)′=−1/√(1−x²) and (8x)′=8, f′(x)=8−15/√(1−x²), matching option e.

after.name: Question 9
after.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of arccosine is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccos}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(15\operatorname{arccos}⁡x+8x) \\  & =15\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccos}⁡x)+8 \\  & =15(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}})+8 \\  & =8-\frac{15}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

a

 21+x2

 121+x2

 21−x2

decision.explanation: The constant 5 differentiates to 0. Since (arccos x)′=−1/√(1−x²), f′(x)=−2(−1/√(1−x²))=2/√(1−x²), matching option e.

after.name: Question 10
after.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of arccosine is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccos}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5-2\operatorname{arccos}⁡x) \\  & =0-2\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccos}⁡x) \\  & =-2(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}) \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 11
after.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of arctangent is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡x)=\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(5x-4)+2) \\  & =\frac{1}{1+{(5x-4)}^{2}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5x-4)+0 \\  & =\frac{1}{1+{(5x-4)}^{2}}\cdot 5 \\  & =\frac{5}{1+{(5x-4)}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Apply the power and chain rules: f′(x)=2 arctan(3e^x)·3e^x/(1+(3e^x)²)=6e^x arctan(3e^x)/(1+9e^{2x}), matching option c.

after.worked_solution:

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡x)=\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({arctan}^{2}⁡(3{e}^{x})) \\  & =2\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3{e}^{x})\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3{e}^{x})) \\  & =2\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3{e}^{x})\cdot \frac{1}{1+{(3{e}^{x})}^{2}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{e}^{x}) \\  & =2\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3{e}^{x})\cdot \frac{1}{1+9{e}^{2x}}\cdot 3{e}^{x} \\  & =\frac{6{e}^{x}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3{e}^{x})}{1+9{e}^{2x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 12

Calculate f′(x) for f(x)=arctan2⁡(3ex).

a
3exarctan⁡(3ex)1+e2x
b
arctan⁡(3ex)1+9e2x
c
6exarctan⁡(3ex)1+9e2x
d
6ex1+9e2x
e
2exarctan⁡(3ex)1+3e2x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The formula for the derivative of arctangent is ddx(arctan⁡x)=11+x2.

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we get f′(x)=ddx(arctan2⁡(3ex))=2arctan⁡(3ex)⋅ddx(arctan⁡(3ex))=2arctan⁡(3ex)⋅11+(3ex)2⋅ddx(3ex)=2arctan⁡(3ex)⋅11+9e2x⋅3ex=6exarctan⁡(3ex)1+9e2x.

content.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of arctangent is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡x)=\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({arctan}^{2}⁡(3{e}^{x})) \\  & =2\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3{e}^{x})\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3{e}^{x})) \\  & =2\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3{e}^{x})\cdot \frac{1}{1+{(3{e}^{x})}^{2}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{e}^{x}) \\  & =2\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3{e}^{x})\cdot \frac{1}{1+9{e}^{2x}}\cdot 3{e}^{x} \\  & =\frac{6{e}^{x}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3{e}^{x})}{1+9{e}^{2x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={f}^{′}(2) \\  & =\frac{6(2)-6}{(2)^{4}-4(2)^{3}+4(2)^{2}+1} \\  & =6.\end{aligned}

before.html:
Question 16
?

Calculate dydx for y=arctan⁡(x3)x6+1.

a
6x2+3x5arctan⁡(x3)(x6+1)2
b
x2−6x6arctan⁡(x3)(x6+1)2
c
3x2+x6arctan⁡(x3)(x6+1)2
d
x3−6x5arctan⁡(x3)(x6+1)2
e
3x2−6x5arctan⁡(x3)(x6+1)2
Submit

decision.explanation: By the quotient rule, y′=[(x⁶+1)·3x²/(1+x⁶)−6x⁵ arctan(x³)]/(x⁶+1)²=[3x²−6x⁵ arctan(x³)]/(x⁶+1)². This matches option e.

after.name: Question 16
after.worked_solution:
Applying the quotient rule, using the formula for the derivative of $\operatorname{arctan}⁡x$ and applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{\operatorname{arctan}⁡({x}^{3})}{{x}^{6}+1}) \\  & =\frac{({x}^{6}+1)\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡({x}^{3}))-\operatorname{arctan}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{6}+1)}{({x}^{6}+1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{({x}^{6}+1)\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{6}+1}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3})-\operatorname{arctan}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot 6{x}^{5}}{({x}^{6}+1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\frac{({x}^{6}+1)(3{x}^{2})}{{x}^{6}+1}-6{x}^{5}\operatorname{arctan}⁡({x}^{3})}{({x}^{6}+1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{3{x}^{2}-6{x}^{5}\operatorname{arctan}⁡({x}^{3})}{({x}^{6}+1)^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate dydx for y=arctan⁡(x3)x6+1.

a
6x2+3x5arctan⁡(x3)(x6+1)2
b
x2−6x6arctan⁡(x3)(x6+1)2
c
3x2+x6arctan⁡(x3)(x6+1)2
d
x3−6x5arctan⁡(x3)(x6+1)2
e
3x2−6x5arctan⁡(x3)(x6+1)2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Applying the quotient rule, using the formula for the derivative of arctan⁡x and applying the chain rule, we get dydx=ddx(arctan⁡(x3)x6+1)=(x6+1)⋅ddx(arctan⁡(x3))−arctan⁡(x3)⋅ddx(x6+1)(x6+1)2=(x6+1)⋅1x6+1⋅ddx(x3)−arctan⁡(x3)⋅6x5(x6+1)2=(x6+1)(3x2)x6+1−6x5arctan⁡(x3)(x6+1)2=3x2−6x5arctan⁡(x3)(x6+1)2.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms the quotient and chain rules give y′=[3x²−6x⁵ arctan(x³)]/(x⁶+1)², matching option e.

content.knowledge_point: Differentiating Inverse Trigonometric Functions Using the Product or Quotient Rule
content.worked_solution:
Applying the quotient rule, using the formula for the derivative of $\operatorname{arctan}⁡x$ and applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{\operatorname{arctan}⁡({x}^{3})}{{x}^{6}+1}) \\  & =\frac{({x}^{6}+1)\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡({x}^{3}))-\operatorname{arctan}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{6}+1)}{({x}^{6}+1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{({x}^{6}+1)\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{6}+1}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3})-\operatorname{arctan}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot 6{x}^{5}}{({x}^{6}+1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\frac{({x}^{6}+1)(3{x}^{2})}{{x}^{6}+1}-6{x}^{5}\operatorname{arctan}⁡({x}^{3})}{({x}^{6}+1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{3{x}^{2}-6{x}^{5}\operatorname{arctan}⁡({x}^{3})}{({x}^{6}+1)^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 17
?

Calculate dydx for y=arccos⁡(x3)ln⁡x.

a
−1ln⁡x1−x6−arccos⁡(x2)xln⁡x
b
−3x2ln⁡x1−x6−arccos⁡(x3)xln2⁡x
c
−x3ln⁡x1−x6−arccos⁡(1)xln2⁡x
d
x3ln⁡x1−x6−arccos⁡(x3)xln2⁡x
e
x3ln⁡x1−x6+arccos⁡(3x2)xln2⁡x
Submit

decision.explanation: Using the quotient rule with u=arccos(x³) and v=ln(x), u′=−3x²/√(1−x⁶) and v′=1/x. Thus y′=−3x²/(ln(x)√(1−x⁶))−arccos(x³)/(x(ln(x))²), matching option b.

after.name: Question 17
after.worked_solution:
Applying the quotient rule, using the formula for the derivative of $\operatorname{arccos}⁡x$ and applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{\operatorname{arccos}⁡({x}^{3})}{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}) & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccos}⁡({x}^{3}))-\operatorname{arccos}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}{{ln}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-({x}^{3})^{2}}})\cdot (3{x}^{2})-\operatorname{arccos}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot \frac{1}{x}}{{ln}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{3{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{6}}}-\frac{\operatorname{arccos}⁡({x}^{3})}{x})}{{ln}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =-\frac{3{x}^{2}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡x\sqrt{1-{x}^{6}}}-\frac{\operatorname{arccos}⁡({x}^{3})}{x{ln}^{2}⁡x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 17
?

Calculate dydx for y=arccos⁡(x3)ln⁡x.

a
−1ln⁡x1−x6−arccos⁡(x2)xln⁡x
b
−3x2ln⁡x1−x6−arccos⁡(x3)xln2⁡x
c
−x3ln⁡x1−x6−arccos⁡(1)xln2⁡x
d
x3ln⁡x1−x6−arccos⁡(x3)xln2⁡x
e
x3ln⁡x1−x6+arccos⁡(3x2)xln2⁡x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Applying the quotient rule, using the formula for the derivative of arccos⁡x and applying the chain rule, we get ddx(arccos⁡(x3)ln⁡x)=ln⁡x⋅ddx(arccos⁡(x3))−arccos⁡(x3)⋅ddx(ln⁡x)ln2⁡x=ln⁡x⋅(−11−(x3)2)⋅(3x2)−arccos⁡(x3)⋅1xln2⁡x=(−3x2ln⁡x1−x6−arccos⁡(x3)x)ln2⁡x=−3x2ln⁡x1−x6−arccos⁡(x3)xln2⁡x.

content.knowledge_point: Differentiating Inverse Trigonometric Functions Using the Product or Quotient Rule
content.worked_solution:
Applying the quotient rule, using the formula for the derivative of $\operatorname{arccos}⁡x$ and applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{\operatorname{arccos}⁡({x}^{3})}{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}) & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccos}⁡({x}^{3}))-\operatorname{arccos}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}{{ln}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-({x}^{3})^{2}}})\cdot (3{x}^{2})-\operatorname{arccos}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot \frac{1}{x}}{{ln}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{3{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{6}}}-\frac{\operatorname{arccos}⁡({x}^{3})}{x})}{{ln}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =-\frac{3{x}^{2}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡x\sqrt{1-{x}^{6}}}-\frac{\operatorname{arccos}⁡({x}^{3})}{x{ln}^{2}⁡x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 18
?

Calculate dydx for y=arcsin⁡xex.

a
1ex1−x2−arcsin⁡xex
b
−ex1−x2+arccos⁡xex
c
11−x2+arcsin⁡xex
d
ex1−x2−arcsin⁡xex
e
1ex1−x2−arccos⁡xex
Submit

decision.explanation: The quotient rule gives y′=[e^x/√(1−x²)−e^x arcsin(x)]/e^{2x}=1/(e^x√(1−x²))−arcsin(x)/e^x, matching option a.

after.name: Question 18
after.worked_solution:
Applying the quotient rule and using the formula for the derivative of $\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x,$  we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x}{{e}^{x}}) & =\frac{{e}^{x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x)-\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x})}{{({e}^{x})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{x}\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}-\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x\cdot {e}^{x}}{{e}^{2x}} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}-\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x)}{{e}^{x}} \\  & =\frac{1}{{e}^{x}\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}-\frac{\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x}{{e}^{x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Differentiating Inverse Trigonometric Functions Using the Product or Quotient Rule
content.worked_solution:
Applying the quotient rule and using the formula for the derivative of $\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x,$  we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x}{{e}^{x}}) & =\frac{{e}^{x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x)-\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x})}{{({e}^{x})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{x}\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}-\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x\cdot {e}^{x}}{{e}^{2x}} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}-\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x)}{{e}^{x}} \\  & =\frac{1}{{e}^{x}\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}-\frac{\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x}{{e}^{x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 19
after.worked_solution:

$$

$$

before.html:
Question 20
?

Find f′(x) if f(x)=arctan2⁡(5x)x2.

a
arctan⁡(5x)10x2(25x2+1)+1x3⋅arctan2⁡(5x)
b
arctan⁡(5x)x2(25x2+1)+2x3⋅arctan2⁡(5x)
c
25arctan⁡(5x)x2(10x2+1)−2x3⋅arctan2⁡(5x)
d
10arctan⁡(5x)x2(25x2+1)−2x3⋅arctan2⁡(5x)
e
10arctan⁡(x)x2(5x2+1)−1x3⋅arctan2⁡(5x)
Submit

decision.explanation: Write f(x)=x⁻²(arctan(5x))². The product and chain rules give f′(x)=10 arctan(5x)/(x²(1+25x²))−2(arctan(5x))²/x³, matching option d.

after.name: Question 20
after.worked_solution:
Applying the quotient rule, using the formula for the derivative of $\operatorname{arctan}⁡x$ and applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[\frac{{arctan}^{2}⁡(5x)}{{x}^{2}}] \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}\cdot 2\cdot \operatorname{arctan}⁡(5x)\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(5x))-(2x){arctan}^{2}⁡(5x)}{{x}^{4}} \\  & =\frac{2{x}^{2}\cdot \operatorname{arctan}⁡(5x)\cdot \frac{5}{1+(5x)^{2}}-(2x){arctan}^{2}⁡(5x)}{{x}^{4}} \\  & =\frac{10\operatorname{arctan}⁡(5x)}{{x}^{2}(25{x}^{2}+1)}-\frac{2}{{x}^{3}}\cdot {arctan}^{2}⁡(5x).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 20

Find f′(x) if f(x)=arctan2⁡(5x)x2.

a
arctan⁡(5x)10x2(25x2+1)+1x3⋅arctan2⁡(5x)
b
arctan⁡(5x)x2(25x2+1)+2x3⋅arctan2⁡(5x)
c
25arctan⁡(5x)x2(10x2+1)−2x3⋅arctan2⁡(5x)
d
10arctan⁡(5x)x2(25x2+1)−2x3⋅arctan2⁡(5x)
e
10arctan⁡(x)x2(5x2+1)−1x3⋅arctan2⁡(5x)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Applying the quotient rule, using the formula for the derivative of arctan⁡x and applying the chain rule, we get

f′(x)=ddx[arctan2⁡(5x)x2]=x2⋅2⋅arctan⁡(5x)⋅ddx(arctan⁡(5x))−(2x)arctan2⁡(5x)x4=2x2⋅arctan⁡(5x)⋅51+(5x)2−(2x)arctan2⁡(5x)x4=10arctan⁡(5x)x2(25x2+1)−2x3⋅arctan2⁡(5x).

content.knowledge_point: Differentiating Inverse Trigonometric Functions Using the Product or Quotient Rule
content.worked_solution:
Applying the quotient rule, using the formula for the derivative of $\operatorname{arctan}⁡x$ and applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[\frac{{arctan}^{2}⁡(5x)}{{x}^{2}}] \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}\cdot 2\cdot \operatorname{arctan}⁡(5x)\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(5x))-(2x){arctan}^{2}⁡(5x)}{{x}^{4}} \\  & =\frac{2{x}^{2}\cdot \operatorname{arctan}⁡(5x)\cdot \frac{5}{1+(5x)^{2}}-(2x){arctan}^{2}⁡(5x)}{{x}^{4}} \\  & =\frac{10\operatorname{arctan}⁡(5x)}{{x}^{2}(25{x}^{2}+1)}-\frac{2}{{x}^{3}}\cdot {arctan}^{2}⁡(5x).\end{aligned}
$$
